## Discovery & Translational Science

- **[Big Pharma]** **Bayer licenses Hansoh's EGFR × cMet bispecific ADC following ESMO 2026 data** [X / Twitter (Jacob Plieth)](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2125892963234406820)
  - Bayer acquired exclusive rights to Hansoh Pharma's bispecific antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) targeting EGFR and cMet in an upfront deal valued at $150 million.
  - The licensing agreement follows clinical data presented at ESMO 2026 evaluating the candidate across solid tumor cohorts.

- **Unleashing E3 ligases for multi-target protein degradation** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41573-026-00190-7)
  - Review detailing structural and chemical strategies to leverage single E3 ubiquitin ligases for the concurrent degradation of multiple disease-relevant protein targets.

- **Generative AI yields dual-targeting degraders of IRAK4 and TYK2** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43095984/)
  - Application of generative AI-driven interpolation across kinase structural space led to the identification of novel small molecules capable of dual IRAK4 and TYK2 degradation for inflammatory indications.

- **Discovery of F73 as a next-generation RET inhibitor overcoming gatekeeper and solvent-front resistance** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43095980/)
  - Preclinical characterization of F73 demonstrates potent inhibition of mutant RET kinases, bypassing both V804M gatekeeper and G810C/R solvent-front resistance mutations.

- **Benzofuran derivatives identified as oral GSPT1 molecular glue degraders for MYC-driven cancers** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43096000/)
  - Discovery and preclinical profiling of novel benzofuran molecular glues targeting GSPT1 degradation demonstrated high potency, selectivity, and oral bioavailability in MYC-dependent tumor models.

- **Reinforcement learning platform generates optimized linkers for FGFR4 PROTACs** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43096004/)
  - A ubiquitination-informed reinforcement learning model enabled automated design of optimized linkers, generating highly potent PROTAC degraders targeting FGFR4.

- **Serum proteomic profiling identifies novel prognostic biomarkers in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.20.26354798)
  - Proteomic analysis across 730 ALS patients using mass spectrometry and Olink PEA identified serum GSN, IGFBP2, and MEGF10 as independent prognostic markers that add predictive value beyond clinical parameters and neurofilament light chain (NfL).

- **Spatial transcriptomic atlas defines recurrent cellular microenvironments in adult gliomas** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.24.26368523)
  - Single-cell spatial transcriptomics of 2.6 million cells across 275 patient samples demonstrated that heterogeneous glioma cell states assemble into conserved cellular microenvironments, such as astrocyte-like (AC-like) neighborhoods, that correlate with specific clinicopathological features.

- **Nipple discharge liquid biopsy detects somatic copy-number variations in early breast cancer** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.24.26365856)
  - Evaluation of a 20-feature somatic copy-number variation panel in nipple discharge DNA yielded 74.4% sensitivity and 94.4% specificity (AUC = 0.863) for breast cancer diagnosis, significantly outperforming plasma cell-free DNA (AUC = 0.517, p < 0.0001).

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **Pilot trial evaluates right-amygdala transcranial focused ultrasound in treatment-resistant GAD** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.24.26368811)
  - A double-blind, sham-controlled pilot study (N = 31) evaluated four sessions of active vs. sham right-amygdala transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) over one month in adults with treatment-resistant generalized anxiety disorder.
  - Active tFUS achieved a 10.33-point reduction in Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) scores compared to 8.81 points with sham, demonstrating safety without meeting statistically significant separation (p = 0.333).

- **Dual-target adaptive deep-brain stimulation tested in Tourette syndrome** [New England Journal of Medicine](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMc2608489)
  - Clinical report evaluating closed-loop, adaptive deep-brain stimulation simultaneously targeting two neural pathways for controlling severe motor and vocal tics in Tourette syndrome.

- **Non-invasive optoacoustic sensing accurately tracks blood glucose dynamics in humans** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.24.26368846)
  - A pilot clinical evaluation of mid-infrared optoacoustic sensing (MiROS) in 30 healthy volunteers undergoing oral glucose tolerance testing demonstrated a mean absolute error of 11.9 mg/dL and a MAPE of 10% relative to reference blood glucose.
  - Over 99.9% of paired measurements fell within consensus error grid zones A and B without transcutaneous needle access.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Big Pharma]** **Giredestrant demonstrates efficacy in ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer** [New England Journal of Medicine](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2608669)
  - Clinical trial results confirm the efficacy of Roche's oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) giredestrant in patients with early-stage ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
  - An accompanying editorial highlights the potential shift toward oral SERDs over standard endocrine regimens in the adjuvant setting.

- **Intensive blood-pressure lowering reduces cardiovascular risk across baseline risk strata** [New England Journal of Medicine](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2607848)
  - Comprehensive clinical trial findings demonstrate consistent reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events with intensive antihypertensive therapy regardless of baseline cardiovascular risk scores.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Biotech]** **FDA approves Cogent's bezuclastinib combination for rare gastrointestinal stromal tumors** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/25/biotech-news-fda-approves-cogents-drug-for-rare-stomach-cancer/)
  - Cogent Biosciences received FDA approval for its targeted kinase inhibitor in combination with Pfizer's **[Big Pharma]** Sutent (sunitinib) for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST).

- **[Biotech]** **FDA extends PDUFA review period for Vertex's povetacicept** [X / Twitter (BioStocks)](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2125744516543971679)
  - The FDA extended its review period for Vertex Pharmaceuticals' dual BAFF/APRIL inhibitor povetacicept following an unannounced information request.
  - Unconfirmed market reports suggest the agency's request may involve protocols surrounding patient IgG level monitoring.

- **FDA advances Rare Disease Framework Initiative to streamline tailored review criteria** [U.S. Food and Drug Administration](http://www.fda.gov/industry/fda-rare-disease-innovation-hub/rare-disease-framework)
  - The FDA and the Reagan-Udall Foundation convened stakeholders to establish a regulatory framework aimed at aligning evidentiary standards with disease progression, population constraints, and clinical feasibility in rare disease development.

- **FDA CDER highlights recent rare disease drug approvals** [U.S. Food and Drug Administration](http://www.fda.gov/about-fda/accelerating-rare-disease-cures-arc-program/rare-disease-drug-approvals)
  - Agency summary details recent rare disease clearances, including Welgemda (ribitol) for LGMD2I/R9, Infilbray (venglustat) for Type 3 Gaucher disease, Lembaz (adrabetadex) for Niemann-Pick disease Type C, Gazyva (obinutuzumab) for primary membranous nephropathy, and Emcitate (tiratricol) for MCT8 deficiency.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **Sanofi acquires Insmed for $41 billion to expand respiratory franchise** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41573-026-00189-0)
  - Sanofi entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Insmed (**[Biotech]**) for $41 billion, securing its commercial and clinical-stage portfolio of late-stage respiratory therapies.

## Public Health & Policy

- **Wastewater genomic surveillance tracks measles virus transmission in South Africa** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04754-3)
  - Whole-genome sequencing of wastewater paired with clinical isolates during the 2024–2025 outbreak in South Africa identified uncaptured inter-provincial transmission chains, validating wastewater surveillance for national viral containment.

- **Primary care shortages restrict healthcare access in major US medical hubs** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/26/primary-care-appointment-times-doctor-shortage/)
  - Widespread primary care physician shortages in major metropolitan areas, including Boston, are leading to extended appointment delays, compromising routine screenings and early intervention pathways.

- **Proposed 2027 Medicare fee schedule cuts prompt concern among medical specialists** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/25/medicare-physician-fee-schedule-change-worry-some-specialists/)
  - Upcoming Medicare payment structure adjustments for 2027 targeting same-day clinical services are projected to lower reimbursement rates for several high-volume outpatient procedures.

**Worth watching:** FDA's pending guidance on required safety monitoring parameters for B-cell depleting and BAFF/APRIL targeted therapies following Vertex's PDUFA extension for povetacicept.

- Biology & Health
    - [Make this Heart Disease Protecting Food even more Potent!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x01cXsOKUnQ) -- Physionic
        - Prospective cohort studies link dietary soy and natto intake to reduced cardiovascular disease mortality, total mortality, disabling dementia, and atrial fibrillation risk.
        - Clinical trials demonstrate that consuming natto alongside viscous vegetables suppresses postprandial glucose and insulin spikes following a meal.
        - Regular natto intake in overweight individuals with impaired glucose tolerance improves insulin sensitivity, lipid metabolism, and markers of oxidative stress.
        - Randomized crossover studies highlight gamma-polyglutamic acid ($\gamma$-PGA) content in natto as a key driver in suppressing early-phase postprandial blood glucose responses.
    - [The Myth of Raising Millions Overnight](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/D35qOd2r-cI) -- Health2Tech
        - Speaker Bret Waters refutes the notion that startup venture capital is raised overnight.
        - Capital acquisition is described as a sustained sales and relationship-building effort rather than a quick transaction.
        - Securing investment typically requires months of continuous dialogue and more than a dozen meetings before funding is finalized.
- Pure Science
    - [Can a roll of tape really make X-rays?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/t81DrYDi3As) -- Veritasium
        - The video investigates the physics topic of whether peeling a roll of sticky tape can generate X-rays.
        - Content is produced by Veritasium focusing on physics concepts and experimental phenomena.
        - The video is sponsored by 80,000 Hours, a nonprofit offering research-backed career advice aimed at tackling major global problems.
